questions.q: What did Michael's speech therapist say was really holding him back?
a: He was too busy planning what to say to listen
He spoke too quickly for people to follow
He lacked the vocabulary for small talk
He was afraid of speaking to groups
questions.why: Lesson 1 says his therapist told him listening, not speaking, was the problem.

questions.q: What does the smart parrot persona ask you to do?
a: Repeat what you heard in your own words
Mimic the other person's accent and tone
Change the subject whenever it stalls
Talk more than the other person does
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes repeating what you heard in your own words.

questions.q: Which follow-up message does the summary suggest sending?
a: Something that made you think of the person
A reminder that they owe you a reply
A request for a favour right away
A list of your available meeting times
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists four follow-ups, including things that remind you of the person.

Names of people whose courage you admire
Tasks you avoid because they scare you

questions.q: What are the three steps of the AAA framework?
a: Acknowledge feelings, accept circumstances, ask what you need
Assess the risk, act quickly, adjust later
Ask questions, answer fully, agree often
Accept praise, avoid blame, advance slowly
questions.why: Lesson 3 names the AAA steps: acknowledge, accept and ask.
